title: Make the verified YEIS path the default while retaining an explicit V2 rollback and automatic runtime fallback

scope.subject: Default universe-engine selection and rollback/fallback semantics

research_summary: Native YEIS now has model, observed-host, Hero, renderer, picking and return-state parity, so keeping V2 as the implicit default preserves migration debt without adding user value. The safest cutover reuses the already-selected YEIS full solution as the default, keeps the existing V2 composite reachable only through an explicit ?engine=v2 rollback, and separates requested engine from active engine so a YEIS initialization failure can fail open to the proven V2 renderer. A permanent dual-engine feature system or external flag service would broaden state and deployment complexity for a single local rollback condition.

sources.finding: The pinned MIT YEIS snapshot is already the selected and locally validated mother engine; the cutover should change selection semantics rather than introduce another engine.
URLSearchParams is a native browser API suitable for a zero-dependency explicit developer rollback query such as ?engine=v2.
React state can represent the active runtime engine independently from the requested URL mode, allowing initialization failure to switch rendering to V2 without a page reload.

search_ladder.conclusion: The verified YEIS full solution already covers the default path; no new full product should be introduced for cutover.
The existing React/R3F shell can switch the active engine as ordinary component state and already hosts both rendering paths.
The existing V2 composite is sufficient as a rollback/fallback subsystem; requested versus active engine state closes failure handling without a new flag framework.
No component package is needed because the browser already supplies URLSearchParams and the project already owns the engine state boundary.

coverage_matrix.capability: YEIS becomes the normal visitor path
coverage_matrix.decision: Select YEIS default now that native parity and runtime validation are complete.

coverage_matrix.capability: one-step rollback when a regression appears
coverage_matrix.decision: Keep ?engine=v2 as an explicit rollback without exposing engine choice as product UI.

coverage_matrix.capability: automatic fail-open if YEIS initialization fails
coverage_matrix.decision: Track active engine separately and switch to V2 in the existing YEIS load error path.
Use one default plus a temporary rollback instead of preserving two first-class product engines.

candidates.name: Default to pinned YEIS; retain ?engine=v2 rollback plus automatic V2 fallback
candidates.source: existing validated YEIS integration + native browser URL parameter
candidates.license: MIT pinned YEIS source; existing project code and data notices unchanged
candidates.reason: Promotes the already-selected mother engine with the smallest reversible change while preserving recovery from both discovered regressions and initialization failure.

candidates.name: Keep the local V2 composite as default and require ?engine=yeis to opt in
candidates.license: project code plus existing donor licences
candidates.reason: Safe locally but leaves the selected mother engine behind an opt-in after its known parity blockers have been closed, extending duplicate-engine debt.

candidates.name: Treat V2 and YEIS as permanent first-class engines with a feature-switch layer
candidates.source: existing dual renderer boundary plus new engine-selection state
candidates.reason: Adds durable state, testing matrix and product semantics to solve a temporary migration rollback need; the global maintenance cost outweighs flexibility.

decision.rationale: Make the already-verified YEIS full solution the default and preserve V2 strictly as an explicit URL rollback plus automatic initialization fallback. This moves the architecture toward one mother engine without deleting recovery capacity in the same change.
decision.fallback: If the default path shows a production regression, use ?engine=v2 immediately; if YEIS initialization throws, activeEngine switches to V2 automatically and the existing V2 galaxy remains available.
